name: Submandibular ganglion
summary: A small parasympathetic ganglion hanging from the lingual nerve above the deep part of the submandibular gland. Preganglionic fibers from the superior salivatory nucleus travel in the facial nerve, leave it as the chorda tympani in the middle ear, join the lingual nerve in the infratemporal fossa and synapse here; postganglionic fibers supply the submandibular and sublingual glands and the minor glands of the floor of the mouth. The chorda tympani also carries taste from the anterior tongue, so lesions of the facial nerve proximal to it reduce both salivation and taste.

anatomy.location: On the hyoglossus muscle below the lingual nerve, above the deep process of the submandibular gland and lateral to the submandibular duct, in the floor of the mouth.

afferents.via: chorda tympani via the lingual nerve

function: Secretomotor supply to the submandibular and sublingual salivary glands.

bestView.label: floor of the mouth region; the ganglion sits on hyoglossus (outside the brain volume)

imaging.normalAppearance: Not identifiable; the submandibular gland and lingual nerve region are seen on neck MRI. Denervated glands atrophy and show fatty change.

pathology.finding: Small fatty gland after chorda tympani or lingual nerve injury.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Neck MRI when a mass is suspected

lesionEffects.deficit: Reduced salivation from the submandibular and sublingual glands
Loss of taste on the anterior two-thirds of the tongue with the same lesion

examination: Taste on the anterior tongue with sugar and salt
pearls: Loss of taste with a facial palsy places the lesion proximal to the chorda tympani, in the mastoid segment or higher
Lingual nerve injury after third molar extraction numbs the tongue and can reduce salivation and taste
